summary: HETA proposes a plausible three-part attribution recipe for decoder-only LMs (causal attention–value gating, Hutchinson/HVP curvature, and KL-under-masking) with unusually broad baselines, models, and robustness checks. The empirical story is undermined by a blocking inconsistency between the DSA definition (normalized masses implying a roughly [-1,1] range) and Table 1 scores up to ~5, plus overclaims that GPT-derived labels are “human annotations.” With metric/definition repair, honest scoping, and tighter method notation, this could become competitive; as written it sits at a borderline reject for ICLR.
strengths: Addresses a real gap: decoder-only, target-conditioned attribution beyond encoder-style first-order methods, with a clear three-component design and component ablations.

Evaluation breadth is above typical: many strong generative attribution baselines, four model scales, Soft-NC/Soft-NS, robustness to noise/syntax/decoding hyperparameters, and efficiency variants (low-rank/window/layer sampling).
Limitations on runtime/memory are acknowledged, and core hyperparameters (β, γ, sequence lengths, hardware) are stated in the main text.

key_concerns.issue: DSA is defined with paragraph-normalized attribution mass (so SciQ-minus-NarrQA should lie in about [-1,1]), yet Table 1 reports HETA scores of 4.25–5.10 and several baselines above 2; the metric–result link is mathematically incoherent as written, so curated-dataset SOTA claims are not credible.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Re-derive DSA precisely (including how SSciQ/SNarrQA are chosen), show a worked numerical example, and regenerate Table 1 so values match the definition; if a different scaling is intended, redefine and re-benchmark all methods under one formula.

key_concerns.issue: Abstract/intro claim alignment with “human annotations,” but gold spans are the intersection of GPT-4o and GPT-5 labels; this inflates trust and conflates model agreement with human ground truth.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Relabel as LLM-consensus (or collect true human annotations on a subset), report agreement with humans if available, and rewrite all “human alignment” claims accordingly.

key_concerns.issue: Final score Attr = MT[i] β S_i + γ I is notationally ambiguous (gate times only the Hessian term vs. gating the whole sum), and β=γ=0.5 is fixed without main-text sensitivity; Soft-NC gaps (~2× next best) look extreme without stress-testing combination/aggregation choices.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Write an unambiguous combination rule, ablate β/γ and gated vs. ungated forms, and verify Soft-NC/Soft-NS under those variants with the same seeds.

key_concerns.issue: Faithfulness tables appear incomplete/uneven (e.g., ReAgent missing for some model blocks in Table 3 while present elsewhere), which weakens the head-to-head SOTA narrative.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Provide a complete method×model×dataset matrix with identical protocol and report means±std for every cell.

key_concerns.issue: Related work is placed after experiments; Motivation overlaps heavily with Related Work; several equations/definitions are hard to parse from the prose.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Move Related Work earlier, tighten Motivation, and clean the MT/HVP/Attr equations and DSA formalization.

questions_for_authors: What is the exact algebraic definition of DSA used to produce Table 1, and can you show one instance where normalized masses yield a score >1?
Is Attr(xi→xT) = MT[i]·(β S_i + γ I_i) or MT[i]·β·S_i + γ·I_i, and how sensitive are Soft-NC/DSA to β, γ, and m in the Hutchinson estimator?
Were all Soft-NC/Soft-NS baselines retuned under the same generative attribution protocol as Zhao & Shan (2024), including identical masking/perturbation budgets?
For LLaMA-3.1-70B, how much do last-six-layer Hessian restriction and HETA-LR+WIN change rankings versus full HETA on the same samples?
What fraction of GPT-consensus support spans would human annotators accept, and does HETA’s F1 hold against humans?
calibration_check: Claims of a new standard and human-aligned SOTA are overscoped relative to evidence: DSA numbers conflict with the stated metric, labels are LLM-not-human, and the fusion rule is under-justified despite strong-looking Soft-NC/Soft-NS tables.

significance.justification: Faithful token attribution for decoder-only LMs is a topic ICLR readers care about, and a working method plus eval suite would be cited, but impact is capped until metric credibility is restored.

novelty.justification: Core pieces (attention–value rollout, Hessian/HVP sensitivity, KL masking) are known; the contribution is a targeted combination and curated probe rather than a sharply new principle.

rigor.justification: Method intent is reasonable and ablations exist, but the DSA definition–table contradiction and ambiguous Attr formula break the claim–evidence chain on a primary contribution axis.

statistical_soundness.justification: Three seeds with small reported std, hyperparameter grids, and multiple robustness metrics are solid; incomplete table cells and an ill-posed DSA still limit confidence in significance of gains.

calibration_honesty.justification: “Human annotations,” “new standard,” and outsized DSA/Soft-NC wins are not scoped to what the manuscript actually measures or can mathematically support.

clarity.justification: Narrative arc is understandable and Figure 1’s caption helps, but equations, DSA formalism, and section ordering (Related Work after Results) impede precise comprehension.

structure_compliance.justification: Contains Abstract, Intro, Method, Experiments, Related Work, Conclusion within a conference-like length, though Motivation/Related Work placement is nonstandard.

reproducibility.justification: Models, datasets, β/γ, lengths, HVP/low-rank/window defaults, and evaluation metrics are described enough to attempt reproduction if code/data links were present; masking scheme and Attr algebra still need tightening.

related_work.justification: Positions against attention, IG, ContextCite, TDD, Peering, and ReAgent with mostly fair limitations; coverage is adequate though somewhat redundant with Motivation.

figure_quality.justification: Captions for the pipeline, component ablations, and robustness panels clearly state comparisons and support the intended claims rather than pure decoration.

breadth_generality.justification: Four decoder-only scales, three public benchmarks plus a controlled set, many baselines, and ablations/robustness sweeps adequately support generality claims for this problem class.

overall_recommendation.justification: Promising system with strong eval breadth but blocking metric inconsistency and overclaiming keep it at borderline reject pending substantial clarification and re-reporting.
